flashcards.q: What are LangChain's base TextSplitter defaults for chunk_size and chunk_overlap?
flashcards.a: chunk_size=4000 characters, chunk_overlap=200 (character-level; most teams override to token counts sized to the embedding model's context limit).

flashcards.q: What is Anthropic's Contextual Retrieval and when was it published?
flashcards.a: Published Sept 19, 2024. Prepends a 50-100 token LLM-generated context sentence to each chunk before embedding and BM25 indexing, so decontextualized chunks ("the company grew 3%") get their missing anchor restored.

flashcards.q: What retrieval failure-rate reduction does Contextual Retrieval achieve, at each stage?
flashcards.a: Baseline 5.7% top-20 failure -> 3.7% with contextual embeddings (35% cut) -> 2.9% with contextual embeddings + BM25 (49% cut) -> 1.9% with reranking added (67% cut).

flashcards.q: What is the one-time cost of Contextual Retrieval with prompt caching?
flashcards.a: $1.02 per million document tokens, assuming 800-token chunks, 8k-token documents, 50 tokens of instruction, 100 tokens of generated context per chunk.

flashcards.q: What is late chunking (Jina AI, arXiv:2409.04701) and how does it differ from contextual retrieval?
flashcards.a: Embed the WHOLE document first with a long-context model (~8k tokens, e.g. jina-embeddings-v2/v3), THEN mean-pool token embeddings within each chunk's span. No LLM call needed, unlike contextual retrieval which uses an LLM to generate an explicit context sentence.

flashcards.q: What is LlamaIndex's SemanticSplitterNodeParser default breakpoint threshold?
flashcards.a: buffer_size=1, breakpoint_percentile_threshold=95 -- cuts occur only at the most severe 5% of sentence-embedding similarity drops.

flashcards.q: What chunk-size starting points make sense for FAQ/support corpora vs narrative/legal/financial documents?
flashcards.a: FAQ/support: 200-500 tokens (answer usually in one paragraph). Narrative/legal/financial: 800-1000 tokens (meaning depends on surrounding clauses). Always validate against a recall@k eval.

flashcards.q: What overlap percentage is a reasonable starting point, and why not more?
flashcards.a: 10-20% of chunk size. Enough to avoid severing a sentence at a boundary; more than that mostly re-embeds duplicate text and dilutes the corpus with near-identical vectors competing for top-k slots.

flashcards.q: Which tools are best for extracting tables from PDFs for RAG, and why?
flashcards.a: Unstructured (open-source + API, detectron2 layout analysis) is the general-purpose industry standard; LlamaParse (vision-based layout analysis) is the stronger choice specifically for complex/merged-cell tables. Both should serialize tables to Markdown, not flatten them to plain text.

flashcards.q: Why shouldn't code be split by character count?
flashcards.a: A character-count split can cut a function or class in half, guaranteeing an unusable retrieval. Use language-aware recursive separators (e.g. LangChain's Language.PYTHON splits before class/def) instead.

flashcards.q: When should you skip RAG/chunking entirely, per Anthropic's own guidance?
flashcards.a: If the knowledge base is under ~200,000 tokens (~500 pages), just put the whole thing in a cached prompt -- no retrieval infrastructure needed.

flashcards.q: What is the "over-compression" failure mode of chunks that are too large?
flashcards.a: A chunk covering multiple subtopics produces one embedding averaged across all of them, so a query about any single subtopic scores lower similarity than it would against a focused chunk -- the vector is diluted.
